subject: Re: DPA execution and non-standard routing: conditional UK addendum / subprocessor gating
messages:
From: Simon Ellis <simon.ellis@oxbridgehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA routing / third-party routing question

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's latest DPA and flagged two items we need to resolve before procurement can sign: 

1) Routing carveout: we require formal confirmation that any third-party subprocessors that process EU personal data will only be invoked from EU-hosted instances unless we agree to an exception. That is effectively an onshore routing requirement that would sit alongside SCCs/UK IDTA.

2) UK signature path: because Oxbridge is UK-based for certain contracts, we need the DPA to be paired with the UK Addendum (IDTA) and for the signature flow to support a dual-acceptance of the addendum (our legal + Redwood). We understand this is covered by your docs but want wording that ties routing gating to the DocuSign envelope (i.e., specific subprocessor activation conditional on signed addendum).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) accept a conditional subprocessor gating clause tied to DocuSign signature state, and (b) provide a short export showing which subprocessors would be on EU-only infra vs global?

I attached our procurement checklist (we will share redlines next). If you prefer a quick call, I can loop procurement.

Regards,
Simon
---
Simon Ellis
Head of Procurement, Oxbridge Health
Attachment: oxbridge_procurement_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Simon Ellis <simon.ellis@oxbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA routing / third-party routing question

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear note. Short answers up-front: yes on a conditional gating approach, with caveats; yes on a subprocessor export, we can produce a scoped snapshot.

High level proposal (so procurement/legal can agree quickly):
- We will add a "subprocessor activation" clause to the DPA that conditions certain third-party integrations on execution of the UK Addendum / DocuSign envelope. That language will explicitly list classes of subprocessors (e.g., analytics, observability, logging) that are subject to the gating.
- For operational clarity, Redwood will provide a time-stamped CSV (attached) that marks each subprocessor as EU-only, EU-preferring (fallback to global only for failover), or global. This snapshot will be included as an annex and updated on cadence (quarterly) or on request for contract lifecycle events.
- We need Laura (Legal) to confirm the precise wording so we don't create an infeasible operational requirement (e.g., blocking security-critical telemetry processors).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Laura / Kimberly to propose 2–3 short sentences to add to the DPA redline that capture the gating mechanics and an annex reference.
2) I will attach the current subprocessor matrix (export) and mark the entries that are candidates for gating.
3) Simon / Oxbridge to review and indicate if any of those candidates cannot be gated (procurement constraints).

If this approach is acceptable I can schedule a 30-minute alignment call with your legal + procurement.

Thanks,
Markus
---
Markus Klein
Director, Sales EMEA | Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_matrix_snapshot.csv (CSV)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Ellis <simon.ellis@oxbridgehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:38:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA routing / third-party routing question

Thanks for the ping, Markus — adding legal context and a suggested draft.

We can accept a gating mechanism tied to a signature state but need to be explicit about three operational exceptions and one lifecycle rule: 

Operational exceptions (we will not gate these):
- Core serving runtime / model hosting (cannot be turned off without breaking service).
- Security telemetry and incident alerting providers (must remain active to meet SLA/incident response).
- Customer-specific on-prem or VPC connectors that the customer provisions (these are outside Redwood-controlled subprocessors).

Lifecycle rule:
- Gating takes effect only after the DocuSign envelope for the UK Addendum is completed by both parties; until then, Redwood will not activate any new non-EU subprocessors for Oxbridge production traffic. Existing global processors that were active prior to signature are grandfathered but must be reviewed and, where feasible, replaced with EU-only alternatives within the mutually agreed remediation window (we can propose 90 days).

Proposed DPA language (short):
"Certain categories of subprocessors shall be subject to activation only upon mutual execution of the UK Addendum (IDTA). Such activation shall be governed by the subprocessor annex referenced in Schedule X and by the activation state recorded in the DocuSign envelope. Notwithstanding the foregoing, subprocessors providing core model serving, mandatory security telemetry, or customer-managed VPC connectors are excluded from activation gating."

Kimberly — please confirm the operational feasibility of a 90-day replacement window for non-compliant global processors flagged by a customer. If 90 days is unrealistic for specific processors, propose alternatives in-line.

Simon — if that language aligns with Oxbridge's risk profile we can insert it into the DPA redline and share a version that references the annex CSV snapshot. We'll also include a short playbook in the annex describing the activation/remediation flow and roles (Redwood ops, Customer security, legal touchpoints).

Laura
---
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
Attachment: suggested_gating_clause.txt (plain text)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA routing / third-party routing question

Simon — looping back after Laura's draft. Good news: legal is comfortable with a gating clause with the operational carveouts noted.

Action items I will take this week:
- Insert Laura's clause into DPA_redline_v3.pdf and return to you with tracked changes by EOD Friday.
- Share a short annex (playbook.md) that walks through: how activation is recorded (DocuSign envelope ID), the ops ticket flow for activation, and the remediation SLA (90 days by default).
- Run the subprocessor snapshot against the Oxbridge risk list you sent and flag any matches for immediate discussion.

Kimberly — please confirm by Thursday if any of the processors in the attached CSV are operationally impossible to replace within 90 days; if so, note the processor name and typical replacement lead time.

Simon — if you'd like, we can lock a 30-minute slot on Thursday 08 Jul at 10:00 BST to walk procurement + legal through the redline and playbook. Alternatively, we'll exchange redlines in writing.

Thanks both — going to get this to a contract-ready state.

Best,
Markus
